settings.editor: Our technicians perform deep-clean evaluations to ensure your systems survive the Middle Tennessee climate. Every visit follows a rigorous multi-point process.

settings.title_text: Clean outside condensing coils and flush/vacuum condensate drain lines.
Test all safety equipment, start capacitors, relays, and compressor contactors.
Verify refrigerant charge levels, evaporator superheat, and air temperature drops.
Inspect evaporator coils, ductwork for leaks, and supply/return plenums.
Calibrate thermostats, tighten electrical connections, and evaluate system amp draw.
Inspect for gas leaks, cracked heat exchangers, and vent pipe integrity.
Clean burners, pilot assemblies, and electronic spark ignition controls.
Adjust manifold pressure and burners for maximum heating efficiency.
Lubricate all moving motor parts and adjust blower belt tension.
Verify complete furnace cycles, temperature rise, and safety control limits.
Flush water heater to clear sediment and test the T&P safety valve.
Calibrate static water pressure to the safe 55-80 PSI range.
Conduct dye tests for silent toilet leaks and evaluate garbage disposal performance.
Survey all exposed pipes, supply lines, and shut-off valves for corrosion or "pitting."
Tag all emergency shut-offs and provide a full system performance report.

items.item_title: Is a maintenance plan worth it for a brand-new AC?
What is the most common plumbing problem in Middle Tennessee?
How often should you do plumbing and HVAC maintenance?
Will an HVAC tune-up lower my electric bill?

settings.editor: Yes, it is essential for protecting your investment. Most major HVAC manufacturers require documented annual professional maintenance to keep your 10-year parts warranty valid. Without proof of service, a single component failure could result in high out-of-pocket repair costs.

The most common issues in our region are sediment buildup in water heaters and high water pressure. Because of the mineral-heavy water in Sumner and Davidson Counties, an annual flush is required to prevent "pitting" and premature tank failure. Our plan specifically targets these local plumbing threats.

You should have your HVAC system serviced twice per year (Spring and Fall) and your plumbing inspected at least once per year. This proactive schedule allows us to catch small refrigerant leaks or high-pressure issues before they lead to catastrophic water damage or total system failure.

Yes, a professionally cleaned and calibrated system consumes significantly less energy to cool and heat your home. By removing dirt from coils and optimizing airflow, we ensure your unit doesn't have to struggle against the Tennessee climate, which directly reduces your monthly utility costs.

Not as a maintenance member. One of the biggest perks of our plan is No Overtime Service Charges, meaning you pay our standard rates for 24/7 emergency calls, even on weekends or holidays. You also receive Priority Service, moving you to the front of the line during extreme weather events.
